message.content:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass in the anterior mediastinum that obscures the left heart border (positive silhouette sign) and displaces adjacent structures, which is the classic radiographic presentation of a thymoma. While lymphomas and germ cell tumors also occur in this compartment, the smooth, lobulated contour and lack of systemic symptoms or calcifications make thymoma the most likely diagnosis among the choices.
